/sdlc accept sha256:1fab5706994daec051dbd183ea42a23ab0e74e2caeefeef1e48454fe17aaa5bb

Authorized account-driven development-test acceptance after actual runtime
validation, not independent Human review, production certification, or Demo Ready.

## Bound delivery and engineering evidence

- Implementation PR #23, protected merge `d361ce032b0f729f62b165c23c4f79bb56f29b92`.
- Exact reviewed head `78e7b75d31c7e83b94b0648de3f770dd07ab84fe`.
- Publish/verify run 36381916918 attempt 2 succeeded, building, publishing,
  pulling the digest, and verifying actual health/dashboard.
- Stage Green 36381621028 attempt 2 and application/container CI 36381621085
  attempt 2 succeeded. All 50 tests pass; lint, build, frozen-blob gate and
  local diagnostics pass.
- Cancelled #8 artifacts and failed PR #14 were not rewritten. New Tests PR #22
  corrected the hook/SQLite observer defects and passed actual controlled Red
  (37 baseline passes, 11 exact failures) before protected merge. Its separate
  48-pass pre-approval harness experiment was not counted as stage Green.
- Operator review removed the new agent's unnecessary exception mutation;
  two supplemental frozen-error tests failed before that focused fix and pass
  afterward. No approved test was changed.

## Actual acceptance observations

- AC-1, AC-6: The actual published image at `http://127.0.0.1:43129/api/ready`
  returns HTTP 200 with exactly `{"status":"ready"}` and
  `Cache-Control: no-store`. Fifty successive real HTTP probes all passed.
  Frozen tests separately prove accessor/summary invocation on every call and
  force-dynamic configuration.
- AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-7, AC-11: A separate container of the SAME digest on
  loopback 43130, with `SERVICE_DESK_DB_PATH=/dev/null/service-desk.db` and NO
  volume, returned exactly HTTP 503 `{"status":"unavailable"}` with no-store.
  Both healthy and faulted instances returned health 200 `{"status":"ok"}`.
  Two faulted readiness requests produced exactly two fixed messages,
  `Service desk readiness check failed`; logs exposed no path, EEXIST,
  exception text or stack. Real tests additionally cover summary-read failure,
  sensitive error content, and frozen initialization/read errors.
- AC-5: The faulted disposable container was stopped and removed by exact ID,
  then recreated from the SAME digest with a repaired usable database
  configuration. Readiness became exact 200/no-store, health remained exact
  200, and dashboard returned 200. No accepted volume was used. This is actual
  configuration repair/restart evidence, not a claim of live environment
  mutation; frozen real file-backed tests separately prove later-call repair.
- AC-8, AC-10: Through the actual browser, assigned INC-0001 to Avery Stone and
  observed matching detail and queue ownership. Read-only SQLite snapshots of
  all four complete rows were identical before/after the 50 readiness probes.
  After a same-volume healthy-container restart, all fields remained identical
  and the owner remained Avery. Browser owner filtering then showed exactly
  INC-0001; unfiltered summary stayed 2 open / 1 in progress / 1 resolved /
  2 high-priority active tickets. All 37 original tests remain Green.
- AC-9: The repaired disposable instance's first readiness request initialized
  and seeded four unassigned rows; its dashboard worked. Real frozen tests
  separately cover legacy-schema migration with fresh read-only observation,
  not merely empty-volume seeding.
- AC-12, AC-13: Actual current-run Red CI 36379790767 attempt 2 passed; complete
  deep assertions executed Green, setup returns no cleanup mock, fresh SQLite
  observers and tracked handles avoid the cancelled attempt's defects.
- AC-14: Reviewed the application's liveness/readiness runbook and followed its
  HTTP probe and private configuration-repair/restart procedure using Linux
  curl equivalents. Exact responses, generic logs, storage isolation, and
  non-production limitations match observed behavior.
- AC-15, AC-16: Healthy, faulted, and repaired instances all used the identical
  recorded digest. Prior ownership runtime/volume on 43128 and earlier demo
  on 43127 remain untouched. No dependencies, shared automation, accessor,
  liveness, ownership contract, or old lifecycle artifact changed.

Only disposable fault/recovery containers were cleaned. Healthy maintenance
runtime and its separate named volume remain on 43129 for inspection. Raw HTTP,
database snapshots, replay inputs, and CI artifacts are retained in operator
session evidence. No production outage, customer benefit, SLO, independent
Human acceptance, or three-run readiness claim is made.
